sentences.text: 4. Initially, the FIR in question was lodged as a missing person report stating that the daughter of the informant was enticed away by the applicant who is also brother-in-law of the victim.
In the statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C., the victim stated that she had gone and stayed with the applicant for 14 years and wrong was done to her.
Similarly, in the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C., she reiterated that she stayed with the applicant for 14 years.
It is also on record that the victim has filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C. in the Family Court, Barabanki claiming that she was kept as a wife.
5. Learned AGA has opposed the bail application.

6. Considering the statements that the victim stayed with the applicant for 14 years coupled with the fact that the victim herself has filed an application under Section 125 Cr.P.C., a clear case for bail is made out in view of Explanation 2 of Section 375 IPC.
As such, the applicant, who is in custody since 08.05.2023 and has no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Ram Janam be released on bail in aforesaid FIR number on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
